So for the congressional ones and stuff, it would be great if those could follow like the actual guide that actual congressional people get."

question: lamontae wants to see real orientation programs for newly elected legislators and decide himself what goes in the game. Answer as one complete set: (1) Congress: the actual orientation and transition the House and Senate give members-elect (the House's New Member Orientation and its handbook, the Senate's equivalent), what it covers, when it happens, and what the member-elect does and receives (office setup, staff hiring allowance, office lottery, ethics and administrative briefings); (2) every state legislature, plus the D.C. Council and Puerto Rico's Legislative Assembly: its orientation for new members, and what a governor-elect or mayor-elect receives; (3) local government: about five representative examples in each of the 50 states, D.C. and Puerto Rico (city councils, county boards, mayors, school boards), chosen to span large and small places. Where a level or place has no program, say so. Then distill the whole set into a short summary written for lamontae: the common elements, how they differ by level and size of place, and the notable unusual cases, so he can choose what the game includes. Nothing is built from this until he chooses.

title: What transition and orientation do newly elected officials actually get
usableAnswer: A per-jurisdiction table for Congress, each state legislature, D.C. and Puerto Rico (program name, sponsor, timing relative to election day, sessions and administrative steps, what the new member receives, citation), about five local examples per state with the same fields, and a one-page distillation for the owner of common elements, differences by level and size, and notable exceptions. Mark a missing program as none, and anything not found as UNKNOWN.
whyItMatters: ChatGPT's A08 said election victory has a transition, not a hidden job-acceptance step. The owner has asked several times for that transition to follow the real guides. Without their content the transition has no steps.
